title: Frozen General-Purpose Audio Foundation Models for Zero-Target-Label Cross-Water Transfer in Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition
content: General-purpose audio foundation models (FMs) are untested for underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) across water areas, where even models trained on underwater audio transfer catastrophically [2]. We benchmark eight public FMs (wav2vec2-base/large, HuBERT-base, WavLM-base+, AST, CLAP-HTSAT, PANNs-CNN14, BEATs) as frozen feature extractors on the four UATR corpora of our series (258,893 segments), both within corpora and in cross-corpus zero-target-label transfer: 12 ordered corpus pairs × 8 models = 96 cells, with probes trained on source labels only (no target labels, no adaptation). Findings: (1) within corpora, frozen FM probes beat the majority-class baseline on macro-F1 in all 32 full-label cells but mostly trail trained ResNet-18 references (the added BEATs encoder edges the trained reference on ShipsEar and leads the FM field on VTUAD macro-F1, while trailing the fine-tuned reference); (2) scale does not help: wav2vec2-large never beats wav2vec2-base on both metrics of any corpus; (3) across corpora, the best frozen-FM probe beats trained-model zero-shot transfer in 11 of 12 directions, and WavLM's Oceanship→QiandaoEar22 probe (macro-F1 0.736) exceeds the supervised target-oracle reference (0.551), yet a 5,000-run permutation control places it at the 96.3rd–97.4th percentile of random readouts (Figure 2), so we report it as a qualified observation, not a superiority claim; (4) a deployable source-validation selection rule beats the trained baseline in 11 of 12 directions, its only failure being o2q, where the winner is invisible from the source side. These are not matched-resource comparisons: frozen FM embeddings provide an adaptation-free, zero-target-label baseline, not a replacement for in-domain training.
